children: Czech manufacturing activity remained in growth territory in September as rising output boosted hiring, although higher costs and supply shortages weighed on production, the S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) showed on Thursday.
The headline PMI figure eased to 53.5 from 54.1 in the previous month, staying above the 50 mark that divides expansion from contraction. It has been above 50 since March.
Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast a reading of 53.9.
The poll showed the fastest rate of hiring workers in more than four years, with output continuing to show growth, as it has done throughout the year already.
But cost pressures worsened, the survey said, impacted by higher energy and fuel prices from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Supplier costs were also affected, firms said.
Companies remained positive in their outlooks for output, according to the survey, and the strength of confidence was above survey trends, S&P Global said.
